question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(X-Y)],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{32}{{\pi }^{2}},\, & 0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{4},\,0\le y\le x; \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y).
$$

Now, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{4},\,0\le y\le x\},$ where $f(x)$ is nonzero.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14154787/assets/ff35a5c562607b4ac314d3ae755156d75baf5d8b01b813f6b59d67dac540e154.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(X-Y)] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{0}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\cdot \frac{32}{{\pi }^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{32}{{\pi }^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{0}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{32}{{\pi }^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}[-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)]_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{32}{{\pi }^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{32}{{\pi }^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{32}{{\pi }^{2}}{[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)]}_{x=0}^{x=\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{32}{{\pi }^{2}}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})] \\  & =\frac{32}{{\pi }^{2}}(1-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{16}{{\pi }^{2}}(2-\sqrt{2}).\end{aligned}
$$
